title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 42-44). Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'tame' analysis situs as a set M of 'lieux' (places). The data are:
- X ≤ Y: inclusion.
- X ≪ Y: 'well inside' (strict or interior inclusion).
- A reflexive, symmetric compatibility relation ≬ ('X and Y are in good position').
- A relation ∥ ('disjoint').
- A dense sub-family Λ ⊂ M of small lieux.
Notation: X̃ = {Z ∈ M : Z ≤ X}; Omb(X) = {Z ∈ M : Z ≪ X} (the 'shadow'); omb_Λ(X) = Omb(X) ∩ Λ. Axiom MΛ5 says: if X ≬ Y and Z ∈ Λ with Z ≪ X and Z ≪ Y, then there is Z' with Z ≪ Z' ≤ X, Y. Equivalently, omb_Λ(X) ∩ omb_Λ(Y) is the union of omb_Λ(Z') over the common sub-lieux Z' ∈ X̃ ∩ Ỹ. Informally, the 'intersection' of X and Y is exhausted by lieux contained in both.

Page 43, first part.
1. Grothendieck takes the relation R, defined from (M, ≤, ≪) alone at the bottom of p.42: R(X,Y) iff for all Z with Z ≪ X and Z ≪ Y there is Z' with Z ≪ Z' ≤ X, Y.
2. He claims (using the right-refinement axiom MΛ1) that R is decreasing: if X' ≤ X and Y' ≤ Y, then R(X,Y) implies R(X',Y').
3. Hence MΛ5 reads ≬ ⊂ R. So the admissible compatibility relations (decreasing, reflexive, symmetric) are exactly those contained in R, and the largest admissible choice is R itself.
4. He notes that ≬ = R in some special situations but not in 'interesting' ones. For lieux in Λ, R holds automatically, whereas in the non-[special] cases there exist lieux that are not compatible.

Page 43, second part (headed 'At C_Λ (type c)').
The aim is to recover ≬ from the disjointness relation ∥ restricted to Λ. Put L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ (the common sub-lieux) and X'_L = X̃' ∩ Omb(L) = {Z ≤ X' : ∃ S ∈ L, Z ≪ S}. Then:
- Claim: X ≬ Y iff for all X' ∈ omb_Λ X and Y' ∈ omb_Λ Y with X'_L = Y'_L = ∅, one has X' ∥ Y'. That is, small pieces of X and of Y that stay away from the common part must be disjoint. Compatibility thus means 'no hidden intersection beyond what common sub-lieux account for'.
- Corollary: if L = ∅, then X ∥ Y iff X' ∥ Y' for all X' ∈ omb_Λ X and Y' ∈ omb_Λ Y. So disjointness is determined by disjointness of the shadows.

Page 44 then asks for axioms MΛ'4 and MΛ'5 on (M, ≤, ≪, Λ, ∥) characterising systems that come from such a structure ('AtD', type c).

Overall purpose: a point-free reconstruction of a topological or tame space from an ordered family of regions with a well-inside relation and a disjointness relation, where Λ plays the role of a basis or of 'points'.
errors: MΛ5 quantifies Z over Λ, but R (as defined at the bottom of p.42) quantifies Z over M. So 'MΛ5 takes the form X≬Y ⇒ R(X,Y)' is literally correct only for the Λ-version R_Λ, or after a density argument using MΛ2/MΛ3 that is not given.

The proof that R is decreasing uses MΛ1. As stated, MΛ1 only applies to Z ∈ Λ, so for R with Z ∈ M the 'on vérifie tout de suite' has a gap: one needs MΛ1 for arbitrary Z, or one should work with R_Λ.

'The largest admissible relation is R itself' requires R to be reflexive, i.e. Z ≪ X ⇒ ∃Z' with Z ≪ Z' ≤ X (an interpolation property). He crossed out 'Cette relation est réflexive symétrique', suggesting he noticed that reflexivity is not automatic.
The characterisation 'X ≬ Y ⟺ …' is stated without proof. The page breaks off (heavy crossings-out, 'L'est un vrai[?]'), and p.44 shifts to looking for axioms rather than proving it.

ideas.what: Axiomatic system of 'lieux' (M, ≤, ≪, ≬, ∥) with a dense sub-family Λ and shadows omb_Λ(X) = {Z ∈ Λ : Z ≪ X}, used to rebuild a space point-free
ideas.modern_name: Abstract bases / continuous information systems; frames with a well-inside relation; region-based (mereo)topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scott (continuous lattices, 1972); Smyth (abstract bases, 1977); de Vries (1962); Sambin (formal topology, 1987); Whitehead/de Laguna/Clarke, Düntsch–Vakarelov (contact algebras)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme (§5); this axiomatics does not.

ideas.what: Compatibility relation R(X,Y): the common shadow of X and Y is exhausted by lieux below both; every decreasing reflexive symmetric compatibility relation is contained in R, and R is the maximal one
ideas.modern_name: Condition that X∧Y exists as a join of common lower elements, relative to ≪ (a 'locally meet-continuous' or coherence condition on a basis)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogues appear in domain theory (Lawson; Gierz et al., Continuous Lattices and Domains)

ideas.what: Recovering the compatibility ≬ from disjointness ∥ on Λ via L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ and X'_L = X̃' ∩ Omb(L); in particular, disjointness of lieux is detected on their Λ-shadows
ideas.modern_name: Contact/disjointness relation determined on a dense basis (as in contact algebras or proximity bases)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of lieux, with well-inside (≪), disjointness (∥), compatibility (≬) and a dense family Λ, is essentially a version of region-based topology (contact or proximity algebras, de Vries algebras) and of abstract bases / formal topology. It was developed independently and contemporaneously with Sambin's formal topology. No link between Grothendieck's tame-topology programme and mereotopology or point-free topology seems to be made in the literature.
missed.quote: Je voudrais maintenant voir que la relation ≬ peut se définir par la connaissance de ∥ sur Λ, par une condition L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could supply a point-free foundation for tame topology or o-minimal-style 'lieux', bridging Grothendieck's Esquisse programme with region-based theories of space and with locale theory.

missed.claim: The characterisation of compatibility via disjointness of shadows avoiding the common part (and its corollary for L = ∅) is stated but not proved. The corresponding axioms MΛ'4–MΛ'5 on p.44 are only begun.
missed.quote: X ≬ Y ⟺ … on a X' ∥ Y'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete small problem: determine under which axioms a disjointness relation on a dense basis determines the 'good intersection' relation.

deep.surprise_reason: These are interesting foundational working notes of an unpublished point-free axiomatics for tame topology. The specific content is routine order-theoretic manipulation, it is incomplete, and it is close to known structures in domain theory and contact algebras.
transcription_corrections: The relation written '≱'/'≯' throughout is the compatibility symbol ≬ (as on p.42), not 'not greater or equal'.
'lol'axiome ML5' is likely '[dit] l'axiome MΛ5 est satisfait jusqu'ici pour cette condition'.
'comb_Λ' should be 'omb_Λ' (shadow), with a struck '∀' before X'.
'si x,y sont dans L' is plausibly 'dans Λ'.
'il [?] existe des lieux x,y qui ne sont compatibles' should be '… qui ne sont pas compatibles'.
The heading of the boxed block is 'At C_Λ (type c)'.
The circled condition at the right end of the box is 'Z ≪ S'.
